title: What Is Sociology? The Sociological Approach
description: Sociology's approach: socialisation, norms, values and roles. Consensus versus conflict perspectives.

title: Classical Sociologists: Durkheim, Marx and Weber
description: The work of Durkheim, Marx and Weber — social solidarity, class conflict and capitalism, verstehen and rationalisation.

title: The Four Sociological Perspectives
description: Functionalism, Marxism, feminism and interactionism — what each says about society and where they disagree.

title: Research Design, Sampling and Types of Data
description: Aims, hypotheses and sampling. Qualitative vs quantitative, primary vs secondary and official statistics.

title: Research Methods: Questionnaires, Interviews and Observation
description: Questionnaires, structured and unstructured interviews, observation methods and the mixed methods approach.

title: Practical and Ethical Issues in Research
description: Practical constraints of time, cost and access. Ethical issues of consent, confidentiality and harm.

title: Functions of Families
description: What do families do? Parsons, Murdock, feminist and Marxist perspectives on the functions of families.

title: Family Forms and Family Diversity
description: Nuclear, extended, reconstituted, lone parent and single sex families. The Rapoports on five types of family diversity.

title: Conjugal Role Relationships
description: Joint and segregated conjugal roles, the domestic division of labour, and Oakley's feminist critique.

title: Changing Relationships Within Families
description: Willmott and Young's symmetrical family, stratified diffusion, and contemporary family issues.

title: Criticisms of Families
description: Isolation, idealisation and marital breakdown. Zaretsky's Marxist and Delphy and Leonard's feminist critiques.

title: Divorce: Patterns, Causes and Consequences
description: Rising divorce since 1945: legal change, secularisation and women's independence. Consequences for families.

title: Researching Families
description: Researching families: surveys, interviews and official statistics. Challenges of studying private family life.

title: Roles and Functions of Education
description: Why schools exist: economy, social cohesion and mobility. Durkheim and Parsons versus Marxist critiques.

title: Types of School and Alternative Provision
description: Comprehensive, grammar, academy and free schools. Home schooling and Illich's de-schooling compared.

title: Education and Capitalism: Bowles and Gintis
description: Bowles and Gintis: correspondence principle, hidden curriculum and meritocracy myth.

title: Factors Affecting Educational Achievement
description: Class, gender and ethnicity shaping attainment. Halsey, Ball, cultural capital and material deprivation.

title: Processes Within Schools
description: Streaming, labelling and the self-fulfilling prophecy. Ball, Willis and competing perspectives on school processes.

title: Researching Education
description: Researching schools: observation, interviews and official statistics. Practical and ethical challenges.

unit: The Sociology of Crime and Deviance
title: The Social Construction of Crime and Deviance
description: What counts as crime vs deviance, and how the same act can be defined differently across time, place and culture.

unit: The Sociology of Crime and Deviance
title: Functionalist and Subcultural Theories: Merton
description: Anomie, strain theory and Merton's five responses to the goals-means gap. How structural pressure produces crime.

unit: The Sociology of Crime and Deviance
title: Interactionist Theory of Crime: Becker and Labelling
description: Becker on labelling, deviant careers and moral entrepreneurs. How labels create and sustain deviance.

unit: The Sociology of Crime and Deviance
title: Social Control: Formal and Informal
description: Formal sanctions via police, courts and prisons; informal sanctions via family and peers. Heidensohn on conformity.

unit: The Sociology of Crime and Deviance
title: Factors Affecting Criminal Behaviour
description: Class, gender, ethnicity and age as factors in offending. Cohen, Carlen and Heidensohn explained.

unit: The Sociology of Crime and Deviance
title: Public Debates About Crime
description: Media, sentencing and young offenders. How public debate about crime is shaped and contested.

unit: The Sociology of Crime and Deviance
title: Data on Crime and the Dark Figure
description: Police statistics, the Crime Survey and victim surveys. Crime patterns and the dark figure of unreported offending.

title: Functionalist Theory of Stratification
description: Davis and Moore on why some roles must be more rewarded than others, and the feminist and Marxist case against.

title: Socio-Economic Class: Marx and Weber
description: Marx on the bourgeoisie and proletariat. Weber on class, status and party — a more complex picture of class.

title: Life Chances
description: How class, gender, ethnicity and disability shape opportunities. Devine on the affluent worker.

title: Poverty as a Social Issue: Townsend and Murray
description: Absolute and relative poverty, material deprivation and culture of poverty. Townsend and Murray compared.

title: Power and Authority: Weber
description: Weber's three types of authority — traditional, charismatic and rational-legal — and sources of power.

title: Power Relationships: Walby on Patriarchy
description: Walby's six structures of patriarchy and how class, gender, race and other factors shape unequal power.

title: Researching Stratification, Crime and Inequality
description: Researching crime and stratification: official statistics, surveys, ethnography and key challenges.
